programme: RBPJ (CSL), the obligate DNA-binding transcription factor of canonical Notch signaling, driving a target set that is itself the Notch output programme — HES1, HEY1, HEY2 (bHLH repressors), NOTCH1 and NOTCH3 (pathway receptors/feedback), NF-κB crosstalk nodes (NFKB2, NFKBIA, TRAF2, CD40), and Notch-driven proliferation targets (MYC, CCND3, MET)
role_in_a: In head and neck squamous cell carcinoma, Notch pathway alterations (dominated by NOTCH1 loss-of-function) are among the most recurrent genomic events, acting largely as a tumor-suppressive/differentiation-promoting axis in stratified epithelium; RBPJ is the transcriptional node that would read out that pathway status, though this specific record carries no direct RBPJ-HNC evidence (Open Targets: no association; no HNC PMID retrieved).
role_in_b: In stroke-relevant cerebrovascular biology, RBPJ/Notch signaling controls vascular remodeling and pericyte-endothelial communication and, through its own target NOTCH3, underlies CADASIL-type cerebral small-vessel disease, the leading monogenic cause of stroke; RBPJ loss also reshapes CNS-resident macrophage states after injury, tying it to post-stroke neuroinflammation.
shared_axis: Both tissue contexts depend on Notch/RBPJ-controlled cell-cell signaling for structural integrity — vascular mural-cell communication in brain vessels versus lateral-inhibition/differentiation control in head-and-neck epithelium — so a network recurrently selecting RBPJ in both settings may be capturing a general 'loss of Notch-dependent tissue-integrity signaling' axis rather than a mechanism specific to this disease pair.
reasoning: RBPJ is exceptionally concordant (120/138) and its target list reconstructs the canonical Notch programme without needing external annotation, so the module itself is solid and independently identifiable. But the retrieved record places RBPJ only in stroke/cerebrovascular literature, not in HNC (Open Targets records no association and no HNC PMID was retrieved for it), so the HNC side of the account rests on field-level Notch pathway knowledge rather than anything retrieved here — hence supported, not established, and moderate rather than strong.
support: PMID 37051908 — Rbpj deficiency disrupts vascular remodeling via apelin/Cdc42 signaling, placing RBPJ mechanistically in cerebrovascular pathology; PMID 36147294 — Rbpj-linked pericyte expansion and impaired pericyte-endothelial communication, a vascular-integrity defect relevant to stroke; PMID 39890825 — Rbpj-deficient CNS-resident macrophage states, linking RBPJ to neuroinflammatory response after brain injury. No PMID in the material places RBPJ, or any other carrying factor, in head and neck cancer.
how_to_falsify: Compare Notch-target activity (HES1/HEY1/HEY2 expression or a Notch reporter, plus NOTCH1/NOTCH3 status) between matched HNC tumor tissue and cerebrovascular/post-stroke tissue from the same patient population set used here; if HNC tissue shows no consistent RBPJ/Notch target dysregulation (e.g., no enrichment of NOTCH1 loss-of-function or de-repressed HES/HEY targets) while stroke tissue does, the shared-axis claim fails and the cross-disease concordance is better explained as a network-inference artifact than as shared Notch biology.
caveats: The tissue pairing (blood|head_neck) means the two disease networks were likely built from different sample sources — probably blood for stroke cohorts and head-and-neck tissue for HNC — so cross-disease TF concordance could partly reflect a shared blood/vascular regulatory backbone rather than disease-matched biology. Only 138 patient-group comparisons drawn from 2 independent cohort pairs limits how much independent replication underlies the 120/138 figure. The tissue-generic exclusion list (IRF8, SPI1, IKZF1, BCL6, MEF2C, and others) shows that the dominant myeloid/lymphoid regulators shared across blood-based diseases were already stripped before ranking, which argues RBPJ's signal is not simply generic blood-TF noise — but the single-view exclusions (GRHL2, RFX2, MEOX1, CREM, HMGXB4, HOXB6, ZNF77, EZH2, MTA2) and the discordant AKNA are a reminder that most of the twelve listed factors, RBPJ aside, do not carry a coherent, literature-anchored story for this pair.
